findings.title: Remote Code Execution via eval() in User Input
findings.description: The application uses eval() on user-supplied input (preTax, afterTax, roth) in app/routes/contributions.js, allowing arbitrary server-side JavaScript execution.
steps_to_exploit: Navigate to the Contributions page.
Submit a payroll contribution form.
Inject malicious JavaScript payloads into the 'preTax' or 'afterTax' fields, such as 'require("fs").readFileSync("/etc/passwd")'.
Observe the server executing the command.
findings.impact: Full server compromise, unauthorized access to system files, and potential remote execution of OS commands.

evidence.quote: const preTax = eval(req.body.preTax); const afterTax = eval(req.body.afterTax); const roth = eval(req.body.roth);

findings.title: Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) on Allocations
findings.description: The allocations endpoint uses the 'userId' from the URL parameter instead of the user's session in app/routes/allocations.js, allowing any logged-in user to access another user's allocation data.
steps_to_exploit: Log in as a regular user.
Navigate to the allocations page.
Change the userId in the URL to another user's ID.
Observe the application displaying the target user's private financial data.
findings.impact: Unauthorized access to sensitive user financial and portfolio data.

findings.title: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) in Research Page
findings.description: The application allows users to supply a base URL which is fetched by the server without any validation, enabling an attacker to query internal network resources.
steps_to_exploit: Navigate to the Research page.
Submit a request with the 'url' parameter set to an internal metadata server (e.g., http://169.254.169.254/).
Observe the server fetching and displaying the content of the internal resource.
findings.impact: Exposure of internal network services, cloud instance metadata, and sensitive configuration data.

findings.title: Unvalidated Redirects
findings.description: The application redirects users to a URL provided via query parameters without validation, allowing attackers to perform phishing attacks.
steps_to_exploit: Craft a URL targeting /learn?url=http://malicious-site.com.
Send this link to a user.
The user is redirected to the attacker's site, appearing to come from the trusted application domain.
findings.impact: Phishing, malware delivery, and credibility loss.

evidence.quote: app.get("/learn", isLoggedIn, (req, res) => { // Insecure way to handle redirects by taking redirect url from query string return res.redirect(req.query.url); });

findings.title: Broken Access Control on Benefits Page
findings.description: The benefits route lacks server-side authorization checks, allowing regular users to access or modify administrator functions despite UI-level hiding.
steps_to_exploit: Log in as a standard user.
Access /benefits directly via browser.
Attempt to update benefit start dates.
Observe that the server processes the unauthorized request.
findings.impact: Unauthorized modification of administrative data and privilege escalation.

evidence.quote: app.get("/benefits", isLoggedIn, benefitsHandler.displayBenefits); app.post("/benefits", isLoggedIn, benefitsHandler.updateBenefits);

findings.title: Missing Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) Protection
findings.description: CSRF middleware is commented out globally, leaving state-changing requests (like profile updates) unprotected.
steps_to_exploit: Host a malicious form on a third-party site targeting the app's /profile endpoint.
Trick a logged-in victim into visiting the site.
The victim's browser sends the forged POST request, updating the user's data.
findings.impact: Unauthorized state changes on behalf of the victim user.

findings.title: Insecure Session Cookie Configuration
findings.description: Session cookies are missing 'httpOnly' and 'secure' flags, and use a default/weak implementation.
steps_to_exploit: Intercept traffic in a network where the application is used.
Access the session cookie, which is readable by scripts (XSS) and transmitted over insecure connections.
findings.impact: Increased risk of session hijacking via XSS or network eavesdropping.

evidence.quote: app.use(session({ secret: cookieSecret, saveUninitialized: true, resave: true }));

findings.title: Unprotected Template Auto-Escaping
findings.description: Swig engine auto-escaping is disabled, increasing the risk of XSS throughout the application.
steps_to_exploit: Inject HTML tags into any field rendered by the template engine.
The tags are rendered directly as raw HTML.
findings.impact: Widespread potential for Stored and Reflected XSS.

findings.title: Log Injection Vulnerability
findings.description: User input is logged directly without sanitization, allowing for log forging and injection of malicious entries into terminal/log output.
steps_to_exploit: Send a request with a malicious username containing newline characters.
The log output now contains a false error message, potentially misleading security auditors.

evidence.quote: console.log("Error: attempt to login with invalid user: ", userName);

code_refs.quote: console.log("Error: attempt to login with invalid user: ", userName);

findings.title: Verbose Error Messages
findings.description: The application renders raw error objects to the user in the error-template, potentially leaking stack traces or database structure information.
steps_to_exploit: Trigger an application error (e.g., malformed ID request).
Observe the error-template display detailed information about the cause.
Gather architectural information from stack traces.

findings.title: NoSQL Injection via $where operator
findings.description: The application uses an unsafe concatenation of user input into a MongoDB $where query in app/data/allocations-dao.js, allowing attackers to inject arbitrary JavaScript to manipulate the database query.
steps_to_exploit: Access the allocations endpoint with a threshold parameter.
Inject a payload like '5'; while(true){}; ' into the 'threshold' query parameter.
The server executes the infinite loop on the database, leading to a Denial of Service.
findings.impact: Data exfiltration, unauthorized access to other users' records, and server-side Denial of Service.

findings.title: Plaintext Password Storage
findings.description: User passwords are stored in plaintext in the database instead of using secure hashing mechanisms.
steps_to_exploit: Access the application's database (e.g., via SQLi or server compromise).
Dump the users collection to see all user passwords clearly visible.
Use these credentials to log in as other users.
findings.impact: Mass account compromise in the event of a database breach.
